status: STEP 1 done and measured. STEP 2 (building OpenConsole from source) stopped: the source build was killed by low memory, and the source reading plus the numbers below show no output pacing in OpenConsole to raise. What it would take is under 'next'.

done.what: Where OpenConsole 1.24 paces VT output to the hosting terminal in ConPTY mode. It does not: since the 2024 rewrite there is no render-thread frame pacing, timer or flush interval on the output path. Every console API call that changes the screen (WriteConsole -> DoWriteConsole -> WriteCharsVT, src/host/_stream.cpp:335-389, and the getset.cpp/directio.cpp/_output.cpp callers) takes a VtIo::Writer, appends VT to a back buffer, and on Submit() calls VtIo::_flushNow (src/host/VtIo.cpp:457-541), which swaps front/back and issues ONE WriteFile of the whole buffer to the output pipe. Writers nest via a cork counter (_corked) so one API call is one WriteFile. The back buffer is freed when over 128 KiB and twice the last write (VtIo.cpp:486). In ConPTY mode no Renderer is created at all (src/host/srvinit.cpp:843, `if (!gci.IsInVtIoMode()) g.pRender = new Renderer(...)`), so there is no render thread
done.evidence: microsoft/terminal branch release-1.24 at 7ff11ee107c984e236960ec948b450ccbc10187b, files and lines as cited; read-only clone in %TEMP%\conhost-lane\term124

done.what: The one knob is the hosting side's pipe. VtIo::_Initialize (VtIo.cpp:92-100) checks the output handle with Utils::HandleWantsOverlappedIo (src/types/utils.cpp:750, NtQueryInformationFile FileModeInformation). If the handle is overlapped, the WriteFile is asynchronous and the host keeps parsing the next API call into the back buffer while the previous write drains (double buffering, at most one write in flight: _flushNow waits on the pending one first). If the handle is synchronous, WriteFile blocks the console host (and the writing program, which is inside its WriteConsole call) until the reader has taken everything that does not fit in the pipe's buffer. Windows Terminal creates its ConPTY pipes with Utils::CreateOverlappedPipe(PIPE_ACCESS_DUPLEX, 128 * 1024) and reads 128 KiB at a time (src/cascadia/TerminalConnection/ConptyConnection.cpp:337, 407, 749). PROTEUS creates them through portable-pty 0.9.0 -> filedescriptor Pipe::new -> CreatePipe(&read, &write, &sa, 0): synchronous, system default buffer size. conpty.dll passes the handles through unchanged (DuplicateHandle, winconpty.cpp:494-495)

`proteus conhost flood|echo|idle` (src/conhost.rs): a self-timing emitter child (64 KiB WriteFile, 80-byte WriteFile or WriteConsoleW; ASCII or SGR-coloured lines) under a pseudo-console made from any conpty.dll + OpenConsole.exe folder loaded by full path (`--host bundled` is the embedded 1.24), over the pipe PROTEUS makes today (`--pipe anon`: CreatePipe, default size, synchronous) or Windows Terminal's kind (`overlapped`: the console's end opened FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, 128 KiB quota), into a reader that discards (`--sink null`) or feeds PROTEUS's parser (`parse`). The child starts through `cmd /c start /wait /b` like the probe tests (a windowed exe gets no console of its own) and a run fails unless every emitted byte came back through the pseudo-console. forge/conhost-matrix.ps1 runs the A/B matrix
done.evidence: 0 failed runs of 72 in the matrix; the first attempt without cmd failed with 'no console (6)' and the byte check, as designed

measured.machine: Core Ultra 9 285H; heavily loaded (other lanes building, memory under 1-2 GB free): spreads are wide, read the ranges not the medians

flood_emitter_mb_s.how: pwsh forge/conhost-matrix.ps1 -Out matrix.jsonl -Other <stock 1.25.261109001 NuGet binaries> (dist copy, PROTEUS_DATA/SOCKET in %TEMP%, sound off); 32 MB per run for 64 KiB writes, 8 MB for 80-byte writes; configurations interleaved, 3 runs each; MB = 10^6 bytes; the figure is the emitter's own payload rate
flood_emitter_mb_s.reading: (1) A program writing 64 KiB at a time gets 10-50 MB/s through stock ConPTY into a discarding reader, far above PROTEUS's 2-3 MB/s 'cmd /c type' figure: that figure is not ConPTY's ceiling. (2) A program writing one 80-byte line per call gets 0.0-1.6 MB/s on every host and pipe: per-call cost (console driver round trip, one parse, one WriteFile per call) is the real ceiling for line-at-a-time output. (3) The overlapped pipe gave the three highest 1.24 runs (54-196 MB/s) but the gain does not repeat on 1.25 or with SGR, and the spread is larger than the effect: not shown. (4) 1.24 against 1.25: no difference outside the spread for 64 KiB writes; 1.25 was ahead in all three 80-byte runs over the anonymous pipe (0.4-0.9 against 0.0-0.3), suggestive only. (5) Feeding PROTEUS's parser instead of discarding did not lower the rate outside the spread.

echo_latency_us.how: proteus conhost echo --host H --pipe P --keys 300 (key written to the input pipe, time until the echoed byte is read back; 8 ms between keys); 3 runs each, interleaved
echo_latency_us.reading: No difference outside the spread between hosts or pipes on this machine today
